from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "What if we want to translate our coordinates back?",
            "We need the inverse of our transition matrix, P.",
            "Multiplying by P-inverse converts our view to Pixel's.",
            "This operation 'undoes' the grid's tilt and stretch.",
            "Now we can communicate back into Pixel's language."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("The Reverse Journey (P-Inverse)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors for lecture highlighting
        colors = [YELLOW, BLUE, GREEN, PINK, ORANGE]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        
        # x = P [x]_B
        eq1 = MathTex(r"\vec{x}", "=", "P", r"[\vec{x}]_B", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(eq1, "A1", "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1])
        )
        
        # derivation: P^-1 x = P^-1 P [x]_B
        eq2 = MathTex(r"P^{-1}", r"\vec{x}", "=", r"P^{-1}", "P", r"[\vec{x}]_B", color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(eq2, "B1", "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # transform eq1 to eq2
        self.play(FadeIn(eq2[0], shift=RIGHT), FadeIn(eq2[3], shift=RIGHT))
        self.play(TransformMatchingShapes(eq1.copy(), eq2))
        self.wait(1)

        # Result: [x]_B = P^-1 x
        eq_final = MathTex(r"[\vec{x}]_B", "=", r"P^{-1}", r"\vec{x}", color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(eq_final, "B1", "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Transform(eq2, eq_final))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2])
        )

        # Show P^-1 matrix
        # Using P = [[2, 1], [1, 2]], so P^-1 = 1/3 * [[2, -1], [-1, 2]]
        p_inv_matrix = MathTex(
            r"P^{-1} = \frac{1}{3} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}",
            color=GREEN
        )
        self.place_in_area(p_inv_matrix, "A4", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(p_inv_matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # Example calculation
        calc = MathTex(
            r"[\vec{x}]_B = P^{-1} \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}",
            color=GREEN
        )
        self.place_in_area(calc, "C4", "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(calc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3])
        )

        # Grid system for visualization
        # We need a small local coordinate system for the grid area D1-F6
        grid_center = self.grid["E2"] + RIGHT * 1.0 # Centered in the D-F block roughly
        
        # Using NumberPlane but restricted in size or manually built
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "D1", "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Standard vector [5, 4] scaled down to fit
        vec_v = Vector([1.6, 1.3], color=YELLOW) # scaled from [5, 4]
        vec_v.shift(plane.get_center())
        vec_label = MathTex(r"\vec{x} = [5, 4]^T", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        vec_label.next_to(vec_v, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(plane), GrowArrow(vec_v), Write(vec_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # "Undoing" the tilt: Apply P^-1 to the whole plane
        # P^-1 = [[2/3, -1/3], [-1/3, 2/3]]
        # We simulate the un-skewing by transforming the plane and vector
        # The vector [5, 4] should end up at [2, 1] relative to the new grid lines.
        
        # Technically, we want to show the plane transforming such that 
        # the basis vectors of B become the standard basis i, j.
        # This is exactly what P^-1 does.
        
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix([[2/3, -1/3], [-1/3, 2/3]]),
            vec_v.animate.apply_matrix([[2/3, -1/3], [-1/3, 2/3]]),
            vec_label.animate.move_to(self.grid["F2"] + DOWN * 0.5), # Reposition label
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4])
        )
        
        final_coord = MathTex(r"[\vec{x}]_B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}", color=ORANGE)
        self.place_in_area(final_coord, "E4", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(final_coord))
        
        # Highlight the result on the transformed plane
        dot = Dot(vec_v.get_end(), color=ORANGE)
        self.play(Create(dot))
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets)
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Calculations based on the provided logic to keep content on the right
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.0
                y = 2.2 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define layout parameters for the Change of Basis lecture
        title_text = "Change of Basis: Seeing the World Through Different Perspectives"
        lecture_lines = [
            "• A 'Basis' provides a coordinate system.",
            "• The standard basis uses i-hat and j-hat.",
            "• Any vector can be written as a combo",
            "  of these basis vectors.",
            "• Changing the basis changes how we",
            "  perceive and describe the same space.",
            "• Transition matrices translate between",
            "  these different perspectives."
        ]
        
        # 1. Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # 2. Setup visual coordinate system (NumberPlane)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"stroke_color": BLUE_A},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        
        # Position the plane on the right side of the screen using the grid
        self.place_at_grid(plane, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # 3. Define Standard Basis Vectors
        origin = plane.get_origin()
        i_hat = Arrow(origin, plane.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=RED)
        j_hat = Arrow(origin, plane.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=GREEN)
        
        i_label = MathTex("\\hat{i}", color=RED).scale(0.8).next_to(i_hat, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_label = MathTex("\\hat{j}", color=GREEN).scale(0.8).next_to(j_hat, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # 4. Display Initial State
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat))
        self.play(Write(i_label), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Define Transformation (Change of Basis)
        # We will transform to a new basis: v1 = [1, 1], v2 = [-1, 1]
        transformation_matrix = [[1, -1], [1, 1]]
        
        # New Labels
        v1_label = MathTex("\\vec{v}_1", color=RED).scale(0.8)
        v2_label = MathTex("\\vec{v}_2", color=GREEN).scale(0.8)

        # 6. Animate Change of Basis
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(transformation_matrix),
            i_hat.animate.apply_matrix(transformation_matrix),
            j_hat.animate.apply_matrix(transformation_matrix),
            FadeOut(i_label),
            FadeOut(j_label),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        
        # Position new labels relative to transformed arrows
        v1_label.next_to(i_hat.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        v2_label.next_to(j_hat.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        self.wait(2)
